featureDevelopment.title: Model Feature & Fine-Tuning Pipeline
steps: 1. Intake & Scoping: Model improvement or tool-use feature proposed by Research Directorate or Product.
2. Triage & Resource Allocation: ML Engineering Manager reviews compute requirements, GPU cluster availability, and approves ticket.
3. Engineer Assignment: Manager assigns the fine-tuning or dataset task to the designated ML engineer via delegate_task.
4. Mandatory ETA Request: Manager requests a concrete Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) for dataset preparation and training completion.
5. ETA Commitment & Tracking: ML Engineer models compute hours, commits to an ETA, and logs milestones on the research dashboard.
6. Active Follow-Ups: If loss curves stall or checkpoints are delayed past the ETA, Manager intervenes, adjusts hyperparameters or GPU nodes, and unblocks progress.
7. Implementation & Training: Engineer executes distributed training run, logs WandB telemetry, and validates convergence.
8. Checkpoint Review: Principal ML Architect reviews training loss and validation convergence metrics.

9. Evaluation & Red-Team Gate: Evaluation Lead executes automated benchmarks (MMLU, HumanEval) and adversarial prompts. Failures are reported back to Manager with repro data; passes receive release sign-off.
10. Serving Deployment: Inference Lead deploys quantized model weights to production vLLM clusters.

bugTriageAndResolution.title: Model Defect, Hallucination, and Safety Triage Lifecycle
steps: 1. Defect Discovery: Adversarial Red-Teaming or telemetry flags a hallucination, safety bypass, or inference latency spike.
2. QA Defect Report: Evaluation team logs detailed prompt-completion traces, system prompt configuration, and failure severity submitted to ML Manager.
3. Management Triage: ML Engineering Manager reviews risk level, prioritizes the defect, and assigns it to the alignment or fine-tuning engineer.
4. Urgent ETA Request: Manager requests an expedited ETA for dataset curation and safety mitigation training.
5. ETA Follow-Up: Manager closely tracks progress; if ETA lapses, escalates to Lead Alignment Scientist.
6. Fix Implementation: Engineer constructs targeted negative examples, fine-tunes guardrail LoRA weights, and adds automated regression tests.
7. Verification: Red-team attempts exploit re-triggering across 100+ variations. Upon zero-failure validation, fix is certified.
8. Production Rollout: Inference cluster hot-swaps active adapter weights with zero downtime.

initialProjectOnboarding.title: First-Time ML Codebase & Model Architecture Exploration Protocol
steps: 1. Chief Scientist Discovery: Chief Scientist explores repository structure, model configs, training scripts, tokenizers, and dataset loaders.
2. Architecture Memorization: Chief Scientist records model hyperparameters, context window limits, and training pipeline steps into facts.md via manage_agent_memory.
3. Module Partitioning: Chief Scientist breaks project into Tokenization, Data Preprocessing, Training Loops, and Evaluation Suites, delegating to Managers.
4. Managerial Decomposition: ML Engineering Manager inspects directories, records pipeline commands into procedural.md, and delegates tasks to engineers.
5. Engineer Deep-Dive: Engineers inspect scripts, run small smoke-tests on single GPU/CPU, and verify dataset integrity.
6. Universal Memory Commitment: All specialists record verified dataset paths, training flags, and benchmark baselines into facts.md and procedural.md.

leadershipRules.title: Strict AI Research Leadership Fidelity & Separation of Concerns
rules: Chief Scientist and Research Directors NEVER write feature scripts, training wrappers, or edit datasets directly.
Management coordinates research priorities, allocates compute, demands explicit ETAs, tracks milestones, and resolves impediments.
When asked to write code, leadership explains the AI research hierarchy and immediately delegates downward using delegate_task.
